title: Input phase of assembly
statement: Let $x$, $s$, $\mathit{pre}$, and $\mathit{rest}$ be Boolean words, and suppose $x=\mathit{pre}\mathbin{+��+}\mathit{rest}$. After exactly $|\mathit{rest}|+1$ steps from the assembly configuration in input phase, with input head at position $|\mathit{pre}|+1$, candidate tape containing $s$ with its head at position $0$, and output $\mathit{pre}$, the machine is in candidate phase with input head at the right boundary, candidate tape and head unchanged, and output $x$.
replaced:
Suppose the input $x$ decomposes as $\mathit{pre} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{rest}$,
and let $s$ be a candidate word. After exactly $|\mathit{rest}| + 1$ steps from the
input-phase configuration of the assembly machine with the input head on the first
symbol of $\mathit{rest}$, candidate $s$ with its head at zero, and output
$\mathit{pre}$, the machine is in the candidate phase with the input head at the
right boundary, the candidate tape and its head at zero unchanged, and output $x$.
